title: Products Not Currently on Sale Using EXCEPT
description:
Find all products that are **not** currently on sale by subtracting the sale product list from the full product list using EXCEPT.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`

**Table: sale_products** — `product_id`, `discount_pct`

Output column: `name`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A'),(2,'Widget B'),(3,'Gadget X'),(4,'Gadget Y'),(5,'Book Alpha'),(6,'Book Beta'),(7,'Shirt Pro'),(8,'Shirt Lite'); CREATE TABLE sale_products (product_id INT, discount_pct INT); INSERT INTO sale_products VALUES (1,10),(3,20),(5,15),(7,25),(2,5);
solution_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM products EXCEPT SELECT product_id FROM sale_products) ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: 8 products; 5 are on sale (ids 1,2,3,5,7); 3 are not on sale (Gadget Y, Book Beta, Shirt Lite)

hints: EXCEPT returns rows from the first query that do not appear in the second query — it is the SQL equivalent of set difference.
You can also achieve this with LEFT JOIN ... WHERE sale_products.product_id IS NULL, but EXCEPT is more concise.
explanation: SELECT id FROM products returns ids 1-8. SELECT product_id FROM sale_products returns 1,2,3,5,7. EXCEPT removes those from the first set, leaving 4,6,8. These correspond to Gadget Y, Book Beta, and Shirt Lite. The outer query fetches their names, giving 3 rows.
